newsitem.title: USA: Emotional Fred Goldman glares at Simpson in court.
newsitem.headline: Emotional Fred Goldman glares at Simpson in court.

text.p: Choking back tears, the father of murder victim Ron Goldman glared at O.J. Simpson across a courtroom on Monday and said there is a hole in his life without his son.

Winding up the plaintiffs' case in a wrongful-death civil trial of a lawsuit brought against former football star Simpson, Fred Goldman told the jury about his relationship with his son, who was stabbed and slashed to death along with Simpson's ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson.
His testimony concluded the plaintiffs' case after six weeks and 65 witnesses. The defence immediately began its case.
Goldman, who has been outspoken in his belief that the ex- football player killed his son, spoke in a shaky voice as family photos of him and his son were projected onto a screen in the courtroom.
At one point his attorney, Daniel Petrocelli, asked his client about a necklace with an Egyptian symbol that Ron Goldman always wore.
"It represents eternal life," he said, breaking down in sobs. Then, turning to his right to glare at Simpson, Goldman said: "He doesn't wear it anymore. Kim (Ron's sister) wears it now."
Several of the jurors appeared to be moved and at least two of them were dabbing at their eyes during Goldman's emotional testimony.
Petrocelli ended with a direct question: "Did you love your son?"
"Oh, God, yes," Goldman replied between sobs.
Asked if he missed him, Goldman said: "More than you can imagine. There's not a day that goes by that I don't think of Ron. It will never, ever be the same again, there is a hole..."
Earlier Goldman said: "We were always close; there was something special about our relationship. Whatever happened, it was a bond that never dissipated."

Simpson, an ex-football star-turned actor, was acquitted in criminal court last year of murdering Ron Goldman and Nicole Brown Simpson. He has been sued in civil court by the victims' families, who contended he was responsible for the deaths and should pay damages.

Speaking about the loss of his only son, Fred Goldman's voice wavered several times when he recalled taking the young Ron and his sister, Kim, on a surprise vacation to Acapulco, Mexico, and when he talked about taking his son to meetings of Indian Guides (a YMCA group for fathers and sons) and Little League baseball games.
